channel.title: doyouknow.app - English
channel.description: Surprising facts about UAE, Saudi Arabia, and the world.

item.title: How Ad Blockers Actually Detect and Remove Ads
item.description: Ad blockers rely on crowdsourced filter lists, CSS hiding, and network request blocking, locked in a constant technical arms race with publishers.

item.title: How Browser Autofill Actually Stores Your Data
item.description: How browser autofill actually stores your name, address, and card details, how it's protected, and the real attack vectors worth knowing about.

item.title: How Dubai Desalinates Water for a Desert City
item.description: Dubai has almost no natural freshwater. Here's how desalination technology turns Gulf seawater into the city's entire water supply.

item.title: How Esports Tournament Prize Pools Get So Large
item.description: Esports prize pools can dwarf traditional sports purses. Here's how crowdfunding, sponsorship, and streaming revenue actually build them.

item.title: How NEOM Airport Is Built for a City That Isn't Finished
item.description: NEOM Airport is being built ahead of the population it will serve. Here's the unusual planning logic behind building transport infrastructure first.

item.title: How Quran Memorization (Hifz) Actually Works
item.description: The traditional methods, cognitive science, and institutions behind hifz, the practice of memorizing the entire Quran, explained factually and neutrally.

item.title: How Saudi Arabia Recruits Talent for Giga-Projects
item.description: How Saudi Arabia attracts international engineers, planners, and specialists for its giga-projects: visas, incentives, partnerships, and challenges.

item.title: How Saudi Arabia's Traffic Violation Point System Works
item.description: A general overview of how traffic violations accumulate against a Saudi driver's license, how Najm fits in, and the shift to automated enforcement.

item.title: How the Saudi Iqama Renewal Process Actually Works
item.description: How Saudi residency permit (Iqama) renewal actually works: the digital process via Absher, sponsor role, insurance requirements, and timing.

item.title: How to Apply for an Egyptian Marriage Certificate as a Foreigner
item.description: A general overview of how foreigners marry in Egypt: required documents, the notary's role, embassy paperwork, and what to verify before applying.

item.title: How to Get a Business License in Egypt
item.description: A practical overview of registering a business in Egypt: legal structures, commercial registry, tax registration, permits, and digitization efforts.

item.title: How Travel Insurance Claims Actually Get Approved or Denied
item.description: Why travel insurance claims get denied more often than travelers expect, what adjusters actually check, and how to protect a claim before you even travel.

item.title: How World Cup Broadcast Rights Are Sold Around the World
item.description: FIFA sells World Cup broadcast rights territory by territory rather than as one global deal. Here's how that market actually works.

item.title: How World Cup Host Cities Were Actually Selected
item.description: How FIFA actually selects World Cup host cities: bid evaluation criteria, stadium and infrastructure scoring, and why some large cities were passed over.

item.title: The Engineering Story Behind the Suez Canal Expansion
item.description: Egypt dug a parallel channel to let ships pass in both directions at once — here's how the Suez Canal expansion was engineered and why it mattered.

item.title: The Real History Behind the Golden Ratio in Design
item.description: What the golden ratio actually is mathematically, why claims it shaped the Parthenon and pyramids are mostly myth, and where it's genuinely used today.

item.title: Why Art Forgeries Are So Hard to Catch
item.description: How art forgers fool experts for decades, the science used to catch them, and why the art market's own structure makes forgery so hard to detect.

item.title: Why the Northern and Southern Lights Appear in Different Colors
item.description: Aurora colors depend on which atmospheric gas gets struck by solar particles and at what altitude, which is why green dominates but red and purple also appear.

item.title: Why Blood Pressure Readings Differ Between Arms
item.description: Why blood pressure often reads differently on your left and right arm, when a small gap is normal, and when a bigger one matters.

item.title: Why Browser Extensions Can Be Riskier Than Apps
item.description: Browser extensions often get sweeping page access with far less vetting than app-store apps, and popular ones can be sold and turned malicious overnight.
